title: Lieb–Robinson locality, clustering and gapped spectral transport

items.title: Weighted interactions and gapped finite-volume paths

references.title: S. Bachmann, S. Michalakis, B. Nachtergaele, and R. Sims, Automorphic Equivalence within Gapped Phases of Quantum Lattice Systems, §§4.1–4.3
Pieter Naaijkens, Quantum Spin Systems on Infinite Lattices, §§3.3–4.1

items.title: Summability and convolution control for lattice weights
items.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, $\Gamma=\mathbb Z^d$, and $d_\infty$ be the max-coordinate metric. For $F(r)=(1+r)^{-d-1}$, $F_a(r)=e^{-ar}F(r)$ with $a>0$, and $F_\rho(r)=(1+r)^{-\rho}$ with $\rho>d$, each weight $G\in\{F_a,F_\rho\}$ is summable on $\Gamma$. Its convolution constant

$$C_G:=\sup_{x,y\in\Gamma} \frac{\sum_{z\in\Gamma}G(d_\infty(x,z))G(d_\infty(z,y))} {G(d_\infty(x,y))}$$

is finite and positive. In particular, for all $x,y\in\Gamma$,

$$\sum_{z\in\Gamma}G(d_\infty(x,z))G(d_\infty(z,y)) \le C_G\,G(d_\infty(x,y)).$$

The constant $C_{F_a}$ may be taken to be the convolution constant $C_F$ of $F$, independently of $a$.

references.title: S. Bachmann, S. Michalakis, B. Nachtergaele, and R. Sims, Automorphic Equivalence within Gapped Phases of Quantum Lattice Systems, §§4.1–4.2
Pieter Naaijkens, Quantum Spin Systems on Infinite Lattices, §§4.1–4.2

items.title: Normalized-trace expectation onto a finite spin region

references.title: S. Bachmann, S. Michalakis, B. Nachtergaele, and R. Sims, Automorphic Equivalence within Gapped Phases of Quantum Lattice Systems, §4.3

items.title: Contractive local expectations and their commutator bound
items.statement:
For every finite $X\subset\mathbb Z^d$, the map $E_X$ of the normalized-trace-expectation definition is a unital positive contraction on $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{loc}}$ and has a unique contractive extension $E_X:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A_X$. For $B\in\mathcal A_Y$, $Y$ finite,

$$\|B-E_X(B)\|\le \sum_{z\in Y\setminus X}\ \sup_{\substack{V\in\mathcal A_{\{z\}}\\V^*V=VV^*=I}} \|[B,V]\|.$$

references.title: S. Bachmann, S. Michalakis, B. Nachtergaele, and R. Sims, Automorphic Equivalence within Gapped Phases of Quantum Lattice Systems, §4.3

items.title: Weighted interaction commutator bound
items.statement:
Let $G$ be either $F_a$, $a>0$, or $F_\rho$, $\rho>d$, as in the weighted-interaction definition. Let $\Phi_u$ be a norm-continuous family of finite interactions on $\mathbb Z^d$, indexed by $u\in[0,T]$, with $M_G:=\sup_{u\in[0,T]}\|\Phi_u\|_G<\infty$. For finite $\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z^d$, define $H_\Lambda(u)=\sum_{\varnothing\ne Z\subseteq\Lambda}\Phi_u(Z)$ and let $U_\Lambda(0)=I$ solve

$$\frac{d}{du}U_\Lambda(u)=-iH_\Lambda(u)U_\Lambda(u)/\hbar.$$

Set $\alpha_u^\Lambda(A)=U_\Lambda(u)^* A U_\Lambda(u)$, extended by the identity outside $\Lambda$. If $A\in\mathcal A_X$, $B\in\mathcal A_Y$ for disjoint finite nonempty $X,Y\subset\Lambda$, then

$$\|[\alpha_u^\Lambda(A),B]\|\le \frac{2\|A\|\|B\|}{C_G} \left(e^{2C_GM_Gu/\hbar}-1\right) \sum_{x\in X,\,y\in Y}G(d_\infty(x,y)).$$

The same estimate holds for the inverse path. In particular, for a constant interaction $\Phi$ evolved in physical time $t$ by $\tau_t^{\Lambda,\Phi}$, take $u=|t|$ and the constant path $\Phi_u=\Phi$ to obtain

$$\|[\tau_t^{\Lambda,\Phi}(A),B]\|\le \frac{2\|A\|\|B\|}{C_G} \left(e^{2C_G\|\Phi\|_G|t|/\hbar}-1\right) \sum_{x\in X,\,y\in Y}G(d_\infty(x,y)).$$

In physical units, $u,T,t$ are times, $M_G$ and $\|\Phi\|_G$ have energy units, and $\hbar$ has energy-times-time units; the weights and convolution constants are dimensionless, so the exponential arguments are dimensionless.

references.title: S. Bachmann, S. Michalakis, B. Nachtergaele, and R. Sims, Automorphic Equivalence within Gapped Phases of Quantum Lattice Systems, Theorem 4.6 and §4.2
Pieter Naaijkens, Quantum Spin Systems on Infinite Lattices, Theorem 4.1.2 and §4.1 proof

items.title: Filtered derivative of an isolated finite-volume band
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $H_\Lambda(s)$ be the finite-volume self-adjoint matrix of a $C^1$ interaction path on the dimensionless parameter $s\in[0,1]$, and let the selected spectral band be a locally fixed spectral cluster, separated from its complement by $\gamma>0$ uniformly in $s$, in the sense of the interaction definition. Choose a positive reference energy $E_0$ and measure physical energies in units of $E_0$; $H_\Lambda$, $H'_\Lambda$, and $\gamma$ in this statement are dimensionless, and the Fourier evolution uses $\hbar=1$. Let $P_\Lambda(s)$ be the orthogonal spectral projection onto that band. Then $P_\Lambda$ is $C^1$. There is a real, odd, integrable function $W_\gamma\in L^1(\mathbb R)$, with Fourier convention

$$\widehat W_\gamma(\omega):=\int_{\mathbb R}W_\gamma(t)e^{it\omega}\,dt,$$

such that $\widehat W_\gamma(\omega)=i/\omega$ whenever $|\omega|\ge\gamma$, and for every integer $N\ge0$ there is $c_N<\infty$ with

$$\int_{|t|>T}|W_\gamma(t)|\,dt\le c_N(1+T)^{-N}\qquad(T\ge0).$$

The finite matrix

$$D_\Lambda(s):=\int_{\mathbb R}W_\gamma(t)e^{itH_\Lambda(s)} H_\Lambda'(s)e^{-itH_\Lambda(s)}\,dt$$

is self-adjoint and satisfies

$$P_\Lambda'(s)=i[D_\Lambda(s),P_\Lambda(s)].$$

references.title: S. Bachmann, S. Michalakis, B. Nachtergaele, and R. Sims, Automorphic Equivalence within Gapped Phases of Quantum Lattice Systems, Proposition 2.4, Lemma 2.6, and Corollary 2.8

items.title: Filtered spectral generators have summable local shells
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and the finite-matrix $C^*$-identity for the local spin algebras. Let $\Phi_s$, $s\in[0,1]$, be a $C^1$ finite-range interaction path on $\mathbb Z^d$, with uniform range, support-cardinality, weighted interaction norm, and weighted derivative norm as in the interaction definition. Assume the selected finite-volume bands along a fixed increasing exhaustion $\Lambda_n\uparrow\mathbb Z^d$ are locally fixed spectral clusters with uniform gap $\gamma>0$. Let

$$D_{\Lambda_n}(s)=\int_{\mathbb R}W_\gamma(t)\, \tau_t^{\Lambda_n,\Phi_s}\!\left(H'_{\Lambda_n}(s)\right)\,dt,$$

where energies are dimensionless ($\hbar=1$) and $W_\gamma$ and the filtered derivative are as in the finite-volume spectral-generator lemma. For every $\rho>d$, there are self-adjoint local interactions $\Psi_{\Lambda_n}(Z,s)$, supported in $Z\subseteq\Lambda_n$, such that

$$D_{\Lambda_n}(s)=\sum_{Z\subseteq\Lambda_n}\Psi_{\Lambda_n}(Z,s),\qquad \sup_n\sup_{s\in[0,1]}\|\Psi_{\Lambda_n}(s)\|_{F_\rho}<\infty.$$

For every fixed finite $Z\subset\mathbb Z^d$, the coefficient $\Psi_{\Lambda_n}(Z,s)$, set to zero when $Z\not\subseteq\Lambda_n$, converges in norm uniformly in $s$ to a self-adjoint $\Psi_\infty(Z,s)$. The limiting interaction has finite $F_\rho$-norm for every $\rho>d$.

For every finite $\Lambda_n$ and support $Z\subseteq\Lambda_n$, the coefficient $s\mapsto\Psi_{\Lambda_n}(Z,s)$ is norm-continuous.

references.title: S. Bachmann, S. Michalakis, B. Nachtergaele, and R. Sims, Automorphic Equivalence within Gapped Phases of Quantum Lattice Systems, Theorem 4.8 and Proposition 5.3
Pieter Naaijkens, Quantum Spin Systems on Infinite Lattices, §§4.1–4.2

items.title: Thermodynamic spectral transport along a uniformly gapped path
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and the finite-matrix $C^*$-identity for the local spin algebras. Let $\Phi_s$, $s\in[0,1]$, be a $C^1$ finite-range interaction path on $\mathbb Z^d$, with uniform range, support-cardinality, $F_a$-interaction norm, and $F_a$-derivative norm for some $a>0$. Let $\Lambda_n$ be any increasing finite exhaustion of $\mathbb Z^d$. Choose a positive reference energy $E_0$ and measure the interaction, Hamiltonians, and gap below in units of $E_0$, so their values are dimensionless and the filtered evolution uses $\hbar=1$; the path parameter, lattice distance, and weights are dimensionless. For each $n$, fix an integer $r_n$ with $1\le r_n<\dim\mathcal H_{\Lambda_n}$, independent of $s$, and let the selected band consist of the lowest $r_n$ eigenvalues of $H_{\Lambda_n}(s)$, counted with multiplicity. Suppose the gap between the $r_n$-th and $(r_n+1)$-st eigenvalues is at least one $\gamma>0$, uniformly in $n,s$. Thus each selected band is a locally fixed spectral cluster in the interaction-definition sense. This includes a finite-volume ground eigenspace when $r_n$ is its constant multiplicity along the path.

Write $P_n(s)$ for the spectral projection onto that band. A finite-volume band state is a positive density matrix $\rho$ on $\mathcal A_{\Lambda_n}$ with $\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda_n}\rho=1$ and $P_n(s)\rho P_n(s)=\rho$. Extend it to a state on the quasi-local algebra by $\omega^\Lambda_\rho(A)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda_n}(\rho E_{\Lambda_n}(A))$, where $E_{\Lambda_n}$ is the normalized-trace expectation. Let $\mathcal S(s)$ be the set of pointwise limits on the quasi-local algebra of subsequences of such band states with $n\to\infty$. If the band is exactly the finite-volume ground eigenspace, $\mathcal S(s)$ is the corresponding limiting ground-state set.

Let $D_n(s)$ be the filtered derivative of $P_n(s)$, in dimensionless energy units, and set $K_\rho:=\sup_{n,s}\|\Psi_{\Lambda_n}(s)\|_{F_\rho}<\infty$, using the local interaction decomposition of the filtered-generator locality lemma. Let $U_n(0)=I$ solve $U_n'(s)=iD_n(s)U_n(s)$, and set $\alpha_{n,s}(A)=U_n(s)^*AU_n(s)$. Then $\alpha_{n,s}(A)$ converges in norm for every local $A$, uniformly in $s\in[0,1]$, to a norm-continuous automorphism $\alpha_s$ of the quasi-local algebra. For disjoint finite local supports $X,Y$,

$$\|[\alpha_s(A),B]\|\le \frac{2\|A\|\|B\|}{C_{F_\rho}} \left(e^{2C_{F_\rho}K_\rho}-1\right) \sum_{x\in X,\,y\in Y}F_\rho(d_\infty(x,y)).$$

The limiting band-state sets are transported by this automorphism:

$$\mathcal S(s)=\{\omega\circ\alpha_s:\omega\in\mathcal S(0)\}.$$

references.title: S. Bachmann, S. Michalakis, B. Nachtergaele, and R. Sims, Automorphic Equivalence within Gapped Phases of Quantum Lattice Systems, §§4.4–5.2
Pieter Naaijkens, Quantum Spin Systems on Infinite Lattices, §§4.1–4.4

title: Lieb–Robinson locality, clustering and gapped spectral transport — Examples

items.title: A one-spin path can close its spectral gap
items.statement: Let one site of $\mathbb Z^d$ have spin dimension $2$, let $Z=\mathrm{diag}(1,-1)$, and define the finite-volume Hamiltonian path $H(s)=(1-2s)Z$ on $0\le s\le1$, with all other interaction terms zero. This is a $C^1$ finite-range path with a uniform finite weighted-interaction norm and gapped endpoint Hamiltonians, but its gap closes at $s=\frac12$. Thus endpoint gaps alone do not imply a uniform path gap.

references.title: S. Bachmann, S. Michalakis, B. Nachtergaele, and R. Sims, Automorphic Equivalence within Gapped Phases of Quantum Lattice Systems, §2 and discussion after Theorem 5.5
